title: The Dog and the Shadow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Dog was crossing a plank bridge over a stream with a piece of meat in his mouth, when he happened to see his own reflection in the water. He thought it was another dog with a piece of meat twice as big; so he let go his own, and flew at the other dog to get the larger piece. But, of course, all that happened was that he got neither; for one was only a shadow, and the other was carried away by the current.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Dog carrying as he crosses the bridge?
options: A bone he found on the road
A stick for playing fetch
A piece of meat in his mouth
A fish caught from the stream

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Dog see in the water?
options: His own reflection
A fish swimming below
Another dog swimming across
A stick floating downstream

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Dog believe about the reflection's piece of meat?
options: That it is the same size as his own
That it belongs to a friendly dog
That it is not real meat at all
That it is twice as big as his own

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Dog do with his own piece of meat?
options: He drops it into his mouth pouch
He lets it go
He hides it under the bridge
He offers to share it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the meat the Dog dropped?
options: It sank straight to the bottom
It was eaten by a fish
It was carried away by the current
It floated safely to the far bank

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much meat does the Dog end up with?
options: None at all
Exactly what he started with
Twice what he started with
Half of what he started with

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Dog lunge at the other dog in the water?
options: He wants to frighten the other dog away
He wants to cross to the other side more quickly
He mistakes the reflection for an old rival
He wants to seize what looks like a larger piece of meat

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistake costs the Dog his own piece of meat?
options: He trusts the other dog to share its meat with him
He fails to realize the other dog is only his own reflection
He drops his meat by accident while crossing the plank
He is pushed into the water by the current

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "shadow" refer to in "one was only a shadow"?
options: A dark patch cast by the bridge
A second, real dog nearby
The Dog's reflection in the water
The current pulling at the meat

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Grasping at more than you have can cost you what you already possess
Dogs should never cross bridges over moving water
Reflections are always larger than the real object
Sharing food is safer than eating it alone

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where is the Dog when he sees his reflection?
options: Standing on the bank of a river
Swimming across a wide lake
Resting beside a well
On a plank bridge over a stream

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Dog do the moment he sees the other dog's meat?
options: He barks a warning at the other dog
He flies at the other dog to seize it
He turns around and walks away
He waits patiently to see what happens

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what carries away the Dog's real piece of meat?
options: A passing bird
Another hungry dog
The current
The wind off the water

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "of course" suggest about the story's outcome?
options: The result was predictable once the Dog was fooled by the reflection
The result surprised even the Dog himself
The result depended entirely on luck
The result was different from what most readers would expect

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Dog's own meat have looked smaller in the reflection?
options: The Dog had already eaten part of it beforehand
The water was too murky to see it properly
The other dog had stolen part of it first
A reflection can distort size and make another portion look bigger

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Dog "flew at" the other dog?
options: He barked loudly at it
He lunged toward it quickly
He swam gently toward it
He backed slowly away from it

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Dog shares his meat with his own reflection
A Dog crosses a bridge safely with his meat intact
A Dog loses his real meat while chasing an imagined bigger piece
A Dog is chased off a bridge by a rival dog
